item.title: Oh My Opencode Quickstart: Install, Configure, Run Ultrawork
item.description: Oh My Opencode turns OpenCode into a multi-agent harness: Sisyphus orchestrating specialists in parallel behind the ultrawork keyword. Install the plugin, verify three things, learn the two concepts that matter — mode switch plus specialist routing — and tune concurrency before billing surprises arrive.

item.title: Oh My Opencode Agents: Sisyphus and the Specialist Crew
item.description: The biggest capability jump in OpenCode comes from separating orchestration, planning, execution, and research into specialist agents. Oh My Opencode packages that into a batteries-included harness: Sisyphus coordinating eleven agents with distinct permissions, prompts, and model preferences — where changing an agent’s model changes which prompt fires.

item.title: Oh My Opencode in Practice: When Orchestration Pays and When It Bills
item.description: Oh My Opencode promises a virtual AI dev team — Sisyphus orchestrating specialists in parallel behind one ultrawork keyword. The promise holds for the right workload and taxes everything else: tripled tokens on single-window tasks, five-figure startup context, and at least one incident where a looping subagent billed hundreds unsupervised. Hands-on results plus community data below.

item.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration Patterns: Six Topologies and How Each Breaks
item.description: Single-agent systems peaked with bounded tasks and one prompt. Production moved on: organizations now run double-digit agent counts, and a large share of multi-agent pilots die within months of deployment. The killer isn’t the idea — it’s picking the wrong coordination topology, or the right one without knowing its failure modes.
